issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs students to create a constructor that follows the attribute order from the UML diagram (the UML lists attributes in the order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation's constructor uses a different parameter order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This mismatch between the specification (UML/instructions) and the provided solution/template can confuse students about the correct constructor signature and cause tests that expect the UML order to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent with the UML and problem instructions. Either (A) update the solution and template constructor signature to match the UML order, e.g. public Lecture(int numberOfInscribedStudents, String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfTutors) and assign fields accordingly, or (B) update the UML/instructions to reflect the constructor parameter order used in the template/solution (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). Ensure tests are adjusted to expect the chosen, consistent order.
